label: copy-phase re-input of b/s/i/a/u/q (necessary, not sufficient)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never in the original or delimiter phases, never at recall_idx 0-1), and only when the input is a repeated token (in_first=0), almost always one of b (40% of mass), s, i, a, u, q. Those tokens give ~93% mass recall, but precision is ~3% because only about 1 in 35 such steps fires. Rate is highest at the final copy step of L=9 sequences (t=17, 4.7%) and at recall_idx 2-3; L=9 holds 75% of the mass, and short sequences (L<=5) almost never fire. A previous input of k/v/u helps a little. Conjunctions of token, previous token, position and length reach at most F1 ~0.20, so the selective factor is not captured by the per-step variables. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.007); the largest are b at the last step of L=9.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=15: b, s, i, a; t=16: b, s, i, a; t=12: b, a, s, i) and the previous input (most: k, v, u, j, w, n; least: o, g, x, 3); timing cues that raise it most: t=17, recall_idx=8, L=9 & t=17.
